label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
**Good software, and nobody to call when it breaks**

One star, for now.

I'm the director of Bridger Bend Community Library in Montana. We're one branch with two full-time staff, a handful of volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. In June 2026 we signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud at $14,200 a year. Our catalog and circulation went live on October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have only worked in offline mode, on one laptop. Our holds queue is gone, roughly 640 holds. Our support ticket has been open 12 days. We've had three replies, and all three said the issue was "escalated to engineering."

Here is what that looks like at the front desk. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up the large-print Westerns he had on hold. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been writing checkouts on index cards like it's 1975.

I want to be fair. The software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. My complaint is with support. Our sales rep promised "a dedicated migration specialist." What we got was a shared inbox.

To Stackhouse: I need a named person to call me this week, someone who owns this problem and can tell me when checkouts and holds will be working again. Our line item is on the agenda at the county budget hearing on November 18, and I expect to be asked how the new system is going. I would like to have a better answer than the one I have today.

To other directors, especially at small libraries: before you sign, ask for support response times in writing. If a salesperson promises you a dedicated anything, get that in writing too. A library our size has no IT department to fall back on. When the system goes down, the vendor's support desk is all we have.

I will revisit this review if Stackhouse fixes the problem.

Director, Bridger Bend Community Library

---

Two things to check before you post: update "12 days" to match the day it goes up, and add your name above the title line if the site doesn't show it. I left out a phone number since Stackhouse has it on your account.
